title: VPC Incremental Stitching and Deterministic Upgrade Acceptance Criteria
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
PRD summary: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a deterministic, incremental upgrade path for Private/VPC deployments where full external egress may be constrained. This work introduces an 'incremental stitching' upgrade model: images and operator changes are staged across subnets/sites with a deterministic handshake and minimal permitted egress for artifact verification. Goal: allow safe, auditable upgrades in air-gapped or restrictive networks while guaranteeing rollback determinism and bounded service impact.

Scope: networking handshake protocol (staged proxy handoff), artifact staging strategy (local mirrors + delta sync), deterministic operator state transitions (precheck -> staged -> commit -> final), and clear failure modes & rollback triggers. Excludes full on-prem installer overhaul and long-lived multi-region data-plane migrations beyond operator lifecycle changes.

Outcomes: 1) Customers in isolated VPCs can apply routine upgrades with zero-unsafe-state windows. 2) SRE/Customer operators have deterministic observability signals and runbooks for upgrade failure scenarios. 3) Minimal permitted egress pattern documented and automatable for compliance reviewers.
acceptance_criteria: Upgrade staging: Images and manifests can be staged to a customer-controlled mirror via a controlled, authenticated delta sync using allowed proxies; full artifact checksums validated locally before install.
Deterministic handshake: Each node/operator reports a deterministic pre-upgrade fingerprint; orchestration will only advance a node to 'staged' if fingerprint and checksum validations pass.
Incremental stitching: Upgrade can be executed in bounded waves (e.g., /24 groups or availability-zone slices) with explicit sequencing metadata and no implicit cross-wave stateful coupling.

Limited egress contract: The upgrade only requires outbound connections to specified hostnames/IP ranges on fixed ports during staging; these egress endpoints are documented and limited to time-boxed windows.

Rollback determinism: If >= X% of nodes in a wave report non-convergent state or critical errors (predefined error classes), automated rollback to prior operator image occurs with verified KV state reconciliation steps.
Canary verification: A canary subset (configurable) validates critical runtime signals (latency, model-serving errors, KV cache integrity) for at least 15 minutes before wave commit.
Observability: Console exposes per-wave metrics (nodes staged, succeeded, failed, rollback reason codes) and an upgrade timeline trace accessible to customer operators and Redwood support.

Chaos-tested: End-to-end test harness reproduces partial-network partitions and validates the upgrade preserves data integrity and does not induce split-brain in control-plane state in >= 90% of randomized trials.
Operator APIs: Public APIs allow customers to simulate prechecks, force a dry-run, and extract artifact fingerprints used during staging (auditability requirement).

Airgap fallback: Where no external egress is permitted, a documented physical/portable-media staging workflow exists with the same checksum and signature verification steps and an operator checklist that maps to automation steps.

Security & KMS: If KMS rotation is part of upgrade, rotation happens in a staged manner with explicit pre- and post-rotation verification steps; keys are not rotated mid-wave without a safepoint snapshot verification.
